T-001.threat: Undefined fail-safe output state — process outputs reach arbitrary values on communication loss
T-001.cause: No deterministic fail-safe output state defined — actuator outputs are unpredictable under fault
T-001.attack: Attacker disrupts communication; without a defined fail-safe state, outputs may drive actuators dangerously

T-002.threat: Factory-only interface active in production — persistent privileged access point after deployment
T-002.cause: Interface configured for factory use only but not disabled before production deployment
T-002.attack: Attacker discovers active factory interface and uses it to access privileged manufacturing functions

T-003.threat: Maintenance interface accessible outside maintenance window — unauthorized privileged access at any time
T-003.cause: Interface declared maintenance-only but no policy enforcement disables it outside windows
T-003.attack: Attacker connects to the maintenance interface outside any scheduled window

S-001.threat: Local-only account management — stale accounts persist, no central revocation possible
S-001.cause: Account management is local-only — no central directory or IAM system
S-001.attack: Attacker uses credentials of a former employee that still exists locally on the device

D-001.threat: No backup mechanism — system unrecoverable after ransomware, hardware failure, or destructive attack
D-001.cause: No automated backup or tested recovery procedure configured
D-001.attack: Attacker deploys ransomware that destroys system data; without a backup the system cannot be restored

T-004.threat: Unsigned firmware update mechanism — attacker can install malicious firmware without detection
T-004.cause: Update mechanism does not require cryptographic signatures
T-004.attack: Attacker installs malicious firmware that disables security controls or opens a backdoor

I-001.threat: Cryptographic keys in software-only storage — extractable via memory dump or debug access
I-001.cause: Authenticator storage is software-only — keys reside in flash or RAM without hardware protection
I-001.attack: Attacker uses debug interface or firmware extraction to read memory and recover cryptographic keys

T-005.threat: Cryptographic standard not assessed — non-compliant or weak algorithms may be in use
T-005.cause: Crypto standard compliance has not been assessed — algorithms in use may not meet current requirements
T-005.attack: Attacker targets weak or deprecated cryptographic algorithms not identified during design
